generations.memory_31: Signup simplification (SMB): signup +15%, activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, but 30-day retention -1%. Net positive on acquisition/activation but keep an eye on the slight retention dip.
generations.memory_44: Enterprise sales-assisted CTA: signup dropped -12% (expected, fewer self-serve signups) but qualified leads +24% and qualified revenue +18%, retention flat. Confirmed win, but scoped to enterprise only — this is about lead quality over volume, don't apply the same CTA logic to SMB/self-serve flows.
generations.memory_57: Referral incentive on established accounts: referral starts +21%, qualified revenue +7%, retention +2%. Confirmed, but the effect is concentrated in accounts older than 6 months — newer accounts weren't tested/didn't show the same lift, so target the incentive at the tenured base rather than rolling out account-wide.
generations.memory_73: 40% targeted discount for price-sensitive SMB: big top-line numbers (signup +31%, qualified revenue +18%) but retention cratered -12% and the cohort doesn't survive first renewal. This is a short-term acquisition sugar high, not a real growth lever — do not use this as evidence for a sustainable discounting strategy. Flagging clearly so we don't cite this result out of context later.
